title: Open scalar comparison with unit, tensor and composition normalization
statement:
Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] and $A\to B$ a map of finite commutative rings. On ordinary unbounded constant-ring pro-etale module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], put $S_T=-\otimes_A^LB$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], let $U_T$ be scalar restriction [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], and use the scalar adjunction [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. Use exact open adjunctions $j_!^R\dashv j_R^{-1}$ [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero] and the canonical $\lambda_j:j_B^{-1}S_X\cong S_Uj_A^{-1}$ [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. The common-right-adjoint comparison defines a B-linear natural isomorphism $\beta_j:S_Xj_!^A\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!^BS_U$. Its inverse is the open adjunct of $\lambda_j^{-1}\circ S_U(\eta_j^A)$. Under scalar restriction and the canonical tensor identifications, beta is the open projection isomorphism at the constant module B [lem-cbc-extension-zero-projection-formula]. For $A\to B\to C$, these beta maps compose to beta for $A\to C$ under balanced scalar associativity [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization], including identities.

For arbitrary $K\in D(U_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ and $Q\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ let $\gamma^R$ be the forward open projection isomorphism $(j_!^RM)\otimes_R^LN\to j_!^R(M\otimes_R^Lj_R^{-1}N)$. The following two routes from $S_X(j_!^AK\otimes_A^LQ)$ to $j_!^B(S_UK\otimes_B^Lj_B^{-1}S_XQ)$ agree: (i) $S_X\gamma^A$, then $\beta_{j,K\otimes j_A^{-1}Q}$, then $j_!^B$ of the scalar monoidal comparison and $\lambda_j^{-1}$; (ii) the scalar monoidal comparison, then $\beta_{j,K}\otimes1$, then $\gamma^B$. Thus beta preserves the unit-normalized open tensor map, for arbitrary Q.

proof.text:
Write $e_R=j_!^R$, $r_R=j_R^{-1}$, $u^R:1	o r_Re_R$ for the open unit, and $
u_T:1	o U_TS_T$ for the scalar unit. Scalar restriction commutes with $r$ by the identified-coefficient inverse-image comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction]. Its scalar mate is $\lambda^{-1}:S_Ur_A	o r_BS_X$ by [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization]. Thus, with the restriction identification understood,
$$U_U(\lambda_N)\,r_A(
u_{X,N})=
u_{U,r_AN}.$$
Here scalar units are the specified insertion $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ of [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] to the two ringed-topos factorizations from $(U,B)$ to $(X,A)$: one changes coefficients on $X$ and then restricts, the other restricts and then changes coefficients on $U$. Their structural ring maps agree. The resulting $\lambda$ is monoidal and respects tensor units; its K-flat balanced map is the same one fixed above. Denote the scalar tensorators by $t_T:S_T(F\otimes_A^LG)	o S_TF\otimes_B^LS_TG$ and the inverse-image tensorators by $a_R:r_R(F\otimes_R^LG)	o r_RF\otimes_R^Lr_RG$.

proof.text:
The exact open adjunctions [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero] and the scalar adjunctions [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction], composed using [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], give, naturally in $K,H$,
$$\operatorname{Hom}_B(S_Xe_AK,H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_A(e_AK,U_XH)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,r_AU_XH)$$
and
$$\operatorname{Hom}_B(e_BS_UK,H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_B(S_UK,r_BH)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,U_Ur_BH).$$
Identify the last objects by step 1. The common-right-adjoint uniqueness theorem [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] supplies the natural isomorphism $\beta:S_Xe_A\to e_BS_U$. All Hom sets here are in module derived categories, so its components are B-linear.

proof.text:
Put $b_K=\beta_K^{-1}$. The unit equation in [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation], with the composite-unit formula [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], says that the scalar adjunct of the open adjunct of $b_K$ is
$$K\xrightarrow{u^A_K}r_Ae_AK\xrightarrow{r_A\nu_{X,e_AK}}r_AU_XS_Xe_AK.$$
On the other hand the scalar adjunct of $\lambda_{e_AK}^{-1}S_U(u^A_K)$ is
$$U_U(\lambda_{e_AK}^{-1})\,U_US_U(u^A_K)\,\nu_{U,K}
=U_U(\lambda_{e_AK}^{-1})\,\nu_{U,r_Ae_AK}\,u^A_K
=r_A(\nu_{X,e_AK})\,u^A_K,$$
by scalar-unit naturality and step 1. Injectivity of the scalar Hom bijection [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] proves
$$r_B(b_K)\,u^B_{S_UK}=\lambda_{e_AK}^{-1}S_U(u^A_K).\tag{*}$$
The open Hom bijection, equivalently [lem-weil-pbc-adjunct-counit-identity], now gives exactly the asserted open adjunct formula for $b$.

proof.text:
For clarity fix the canonical open projection normalization: put $\delta^R_{M,N}=(\gamma^R_{M,N})^{-1}$. The canonical map in [lem-cbc-extension-zero-projection-formula] has inverse the open adjunct of
$$M\otimes_R^Lr_RN\xrightarrow{u^R_M\otimes1}r_Re_RM\otimes_R^Lr_RN\xrightarrow{a_R^{-1}}r_R(e_RM\otimes_R^LN).\tag{**}$$
This describes the canonical map, rather than choosing an isomorphism of its endpoints: in the Hom calculation of sites-modules.tex Tag 0E8I it is the image of the identity, and its derived version is Tag 0GL1. The derived open adjunction used here is [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]; the tensorators and unitors are those of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]. We will compare morphisms by this open Hom bijection [lem-weil-pbc-adjunct-counit-identity].

proof.text:
Restrict (*) to A-modules. Identify $U_TS_TF$ with $F\otimes_A^LB_T$: both are computed by the same tensor of a K-flat representative in [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], forgetting only the target-ring action [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Identify $U_Xe_B$ with $e_AU_U$ by [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]. The open units agree under this identification: they are the termwise extension/restriction units, identity on sections over U, and scalar restriction changes only the ring action. In these identifications the right side of (*) is
$$K\otimes_A^LB_U\xrightarrow{u^A_K\otimes1}r_Ae_AK\otimes_A^LB_U\xrightarrow{a_A^{-1}}r_A(e_AK\otimes_A^LB_X).$$
Indeed the balanced pullback comparison retains the B factor, and scalar extension sends a morphism to its tensor with $1_B$; these are the K-flat maps fixed in [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization]. By (**) and injectivity of the open Hom bijection, $U_Xb$ is $\delta^A_{K,B_X}$. Inverting proves that the restricted $\beta$ is exactly $\gamma^A_{K,B_X}$.

proof.text:
For $A\to B\to C$, write $\alpha_T:S_T^{B,C}S_T^{A,B}\to S_T^{A,C}$ for [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization]. Consider
$$e_CS_U^{A,C}\xrightarrow{e_C\alpha_U^{-1}}e_CS_U^{B,C}S_U^{A,B}\xrightarrow{b^{B,C}_{S_U^{A,B}K}}S_X^{B,C}e_BS_U^{A,B}\xrightarrow{S_X^{B,C}b^{A,B}_K}S_X^{B,C}S_X^{A,B}e_A\xrightarrow{\alpha_X}S_X^{A,C}e_A.$$
Its common-right-adjoint Hom correspondence is the two scalar Hom bijections with the open Hom bijection moved past each in turn. The coefficient-unit clause of [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization] identifies the two successive scalar bijections with the single one for $A\to C$: expanding the composite units [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] inserts $x\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes1\mapsto x\otimes1$. Restriction changes the action by the composite ring map on both sides [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Thus the displayed map and $b^{A,C}$ have the same unit equation, and uniqueness [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] identifies them. For an identity ring map the same computation uses $x\otimes a\mapsto ax$ and the tensor unitor, giving identity $b$. Inverting gives the asserted coefficient cocycle and identities for $\beta$.

proof.text:
To prove the mixed tensor square, it suffices to prove its inverse form. Suppress only canonical associators and write $K\otimes r_AQ$ for $K\otimes_A^Lr_AQ$. The required inverse equality is
$$S_X(\delta^A_{K,Q})\,b_{K\otimes r_AQ}\,e_B\bigl(t_U^{-1}(1\otimes\lambda_Q)\bigr)
=t_X^{-1}(b_K\otimes1)\,\delta^B_{S_UK,S_XQ}.\tag{***}$$
Both sides have source $e_B(S_UK\otimes_B^Lr_BS_XQ)$ and target $S_X(e_AK\otimes_A^LQ)$. Take the open adjunct, using [lem-weil-pbc-adjunct-counit-identity]. By (**) the adjunct of the right side is
$$r_B(t_X^{-1})\,a_B^{-1}\bigl((r_Bb_K\,u^B_{S_UK})\otimes1\bigr)
=r_B(t_X^{-1})\,a_B^{-1}\bigl((\lambda_{e_AK}^{-1}S_Uu^A_K)\otimes1\bigr),\tag{J}$$
where the first equality uses naturality of $a_B$ and the second uses (*). These are equalities of derived morphisms, not tests on ordinary geometric stalks.

proof.text:
The adjunct of the left side of (***) is, by naturality of the open unit and (*) at $K\otimes r_AQ$,
$$r_BS_X(\delta^A_{K,Q})\,\lambda_{e_A(K\otimes r_AQ)}^{-1}S_U(u^A_{K\otimes r_AQ})\,t_U^{-1}(1\otimes\lambda_Q).$$
Naturality of $\lambda$ moves its inverse to the left. Equation (**) replaces $r_A(\delta^A)u^A$ by $a_A^{-1}(u^A_K\otimes1)$. The result is
$$\lambda_{e_AK\otimes Q}^{-1}S_U(a_A^{-1})S_U(u^A_K\otimes1)\,t_U^{-1}(1\otimes\lambda_Q).$$
Tensorator naturality moves $S_U(u^A_K\otimes1)$ through $t_U^{-1}$. Monoidality of $\lambda$ from [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] then replaces
$$\lambda_{F\otimes Q}^{-1}S_U(a_A^{-1})t_U^{-1}
\quad\text{by}\quad r_B(t_X^{-1})a_B^{-1}(\lambda_F^{-1}\otimes\lambda_Q^{-1}),\qquad F=e_AK.$$
Cancel $\lambda_Q^{-1}\lambda_Q$. This is exactly (J). Injectivity of the open Hom bijection [lem-weil-pbc-adjunct-counit-identity] proves (***). All maps in (***) are isomorphisms by steps 1--4; invert the equality to obtain the two forward routes in the statement for arbitrary K and Q. Unitor coherence in [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] includes the unit-normalized case. No boundedness, flatness of $A\to B$, or quasi-compactness of j has entered.

No SGA source, no cycle (item absent from the 2929-node dep closure), and no re-split note. Steps 1–8 re-derived with all directions written out. (1) λ^{-1} is the scalar mate of r_A U_X = U_U r_B (K-flat node), so ν_U = U_U(λ) r_A ν_X; λ is monoidal as c'∘c^{-1} of the two ringed-topos factorisations of (U,B)→(X,A) (monoidal-comparisons node). (2–3) The conjugate lemma applies with L1 = S_X e_A, L2 = e_B S_U. Composite units plus scalar-unit naturality give (*): r_B(b) u^B = λ^{-1} S_U(u^A). (4) (**) matches the Yoneda chain of Stacks 0E8I (sites-modules l.4051), the projection-formula node's imported proof, and the reviewed lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization. Advisory only: the step reads which canonical map is meant from the source. (5) U_X b = δ^A_{K,B_X} follows from the restriction/extension identification and the tensorator a_A. (6) The cocycle follows by pasting conjugates, then the successive-quotient units and uniqueness; the identity case works. (7–8) (***) is exactly the inverse of routes (i)/(ii). (J) and the left-side reduction agree after using λ-monoidality as t_U S_U(a_A) λ = (λ⊗λ) a_B r_B(t_X); no symmetry is used, so no sign.
